experiment: E2.c config-RL: does a GRPO policy learn to select scan_mode/chunk_len per shape?
box: gpu-flash-mamba-rl a4-highgpu-8g 8xB200 spot, europe-north1-b (relocated from us-east1-b via snapshot)

run.baseline: shipped serial-default heuristic (speedup measured vs it, same path as the RL reward)

saturated_mode_check.note: best-tuned serial vs best-tuned chunk_parallel at b8/L2048/d2048, scored through the same score_config_candidate path (driver scratch/e2_mode_check.py). speedup is vs the shipped serial default.

verdict.policy_learned: chunk_parallel at every level (100% of late-step emissions); serial was never sampled
verdict.crossover_hypothesis: FALSIFIED -- no shape-dependent serial<->chunk_parallel crossover survives joint chunk_len tuning. The follow-up mode-check shows tuned chunk_parallel >= best-tuned serial even at the saturated shape for BOTH backward ops. The prior rigor's 'serial best at saturated (chunk_parallel 0.85x)' was an artifact of a fixed/untuned chunk_len; with chunk_len~256 chunk_parallel wins everywhere tested.
verdict.caveat: The policy never explored serial (narrow exploration at temperature 1.1), so this run alone shows 'commits to chunk_parallel, reward-optimal' rather than 'weighed serial and rejected it'. The independent mode-check confirms chunk_parallel is in fact optimal, so the policy's commitment is reward-correct.
verdict.implication: chunk_parallel + chunk_len~256 + num_warps=4 is a candidate NEW DEFAULT for these SISO ops -- it beats the well-tuned shipped serial kernel at every tested shape incl saturated. Needs a broader shape sweep before changing the shipped default.
verdict.asset3: Config-RL (RL-as-autotuner) genuinely beats the shipped hand-written kernel at all 6 shapes; all configs contract-clean (full gate battery per config, bug-routing bonus on the #904 backward ops).
